text:
**Short answer:** A pellet smoker draws very little once it's lit, so a roughly 1 kWh power station with a decent surge rating will cover one overnight cook. My top pick is the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2**.

**Why a pellet smoker is easy to power**
- The auger, fan and controller draw only about 35–60 W. Only the igniter pulls 200–400 W, and only for the first few minutes ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- One measured run, a Z Grills on a Jackery Explorer 1000, used 210 Wh in 6 hours. That works out to about 450–750 Wh for a full overnight cook ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- Volt & Valley says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook, and the inverter's surge rating matters more than capacity ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)).
- BLUETTI's own guide is more conservative and assumes 150–250 W average draw ([BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker)). If your grill runs hotter than most, size up.

**My pick: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899)**
- It has 2,073.6 Wh and a 2,600 W inverter. Dealectric says that covers two or three 12-hour cooks and handles the igniter easily ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- That's enough for a weekend at a campsite without recharging. It was listed in stock on 2026-11-04.
- [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). The link pre-applies the code DEALECTRIC, which the page says saves $44.95.
- Dealectric sells this and is the source of that pricing, so treat it as a retailer's recommendation. Its sizing math does match the independent Volt & Valley numbers.

**Cheaper alternatives**
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, $449): it handles one overnight cook. The page says it's back in stock in late November ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W): it's in the same class as the AC180. Price and stock are on Amazon ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh, 600 W, $289.99): this is only about 5 hours of a 35 W smoker, so it won't last overnight. Volt & Valley says 288 Wh covers roughly five hours.

**What to avoid**
- **300 W inverters:** these are marginal. Volt & Valley says a 300 W continuous / 600 W surge unit may not handle an igniter drawing 350–500 W ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)). That rules out the EcoFlow RIVER 3, for example.
- **Don't size for an electric smoker.** One result says electric smokers draw about 1,000 W and need 10,000 Wh for 8 hours ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/)). That doesn't apply to a pellet smoker.
- **The Grilla Power Station** ($359.99) is a 300 W unit with a claimed 10-hour runtime ([Grilla](https://www.grillagrills.com/product/1197809)). It's made for Grilla's own grills, and the 300 W output is the igniter risk above. I'd check compatibility before buying.

**Before you go**
- Check your grill's data plate for igniter wattage.
- Run a full startup-to-shutdown test with a watt meter ([GearBrain video](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill)).
- Allow extra capacity if you're also charging phones or running lights from the same battery.
- Keep the battery dry and clear of heat, grease and ash.
